critique.evidence: The headline, subtitle, selected-row treatment, and side-by-side “LEGACY STEP_UP” versus “INTENT INTEGRITY ALLOW” result make the central comparison understandable on desktop. The instruction explicitly says to select a cached transaction. However, the table’s generic DECISION value says ALLOW for the selected event while its detail says legacy STEP_UP, without identifying which policy the table column represents. “Credentials and amount checks pass” also does not explain why legacy requires a step-up. On tablet and mobile, the comparison appears only after all eight rows, so selection and outcome are separated by a long scroll; mobile labels and evidence text are also very small. These ambiguities keep it below demo-ready clarity.
critique.fix: Label the table result by policy, or show both decisions in each row, and rewrite the legacy rationale to state the precise trigger for STEP_UP. On tablet/mobile, place the selected transaction comparison directly beneath the tapped row or in a sticky/detail drawer, with larger supporting text and an explicit “Tap a transaction to compare policies” prompt.
